### Problem

The release lane cannot pass while the test repository serialises its scenarios, mistakes them for duplicates, refuses their commits and never checks the fork's pull request, so no engine release can be tagged.

### Scope

- kinds/engine-test/pack.yml: the test repository's `core` and the fixed change's `file`, so that only `core-one-at-a-time` writes under the core.
- scripts/release-scenarios.py and tests/release/scenarios.yml: each scenario's issue carries its scenario id in its title and body; every file a scenario writes goes through the GraphQL mutation `createCommitOnBranch` instead of the contents API.
- fork-without-secrets: why the conventions check never reports on the fork's pull request, and its fix or the scenario's right wait.

### Out of scope

- The organisation's signed-commits ruleset: it stays as it is.
- The test identity's account and token.

### Acceptance criteria

- C1: Given the scenarios played in parallel, when any scenario but `core-one-at-a-time` gets its fixed change, then its issue never carries `autopilot:core-wait`, tested in release-scenarios.py --test from the pack.
- C2: Given two scenarios played at once, when triage reads their issues, then neither is labelled `duplicate`, because each title and body carries its own scenario id, tested in release-scenarios.py --test.
- C3: Given a scenario that writes a file in the test repository, when it writes it, then it uses `createCommitOnBranch` and no `PUT .../contents/` call is left in release-scenarios.py, tested in release-scenarios.py --test.
- C4: Given `fork-without-secrets`, when the fork's pull request is opened, then the scenario sees its conventions check report, or waits for what the fork's run really does, tested in release-scenarios.py --test.
- C5: Given the candidate with this fix, when the release lane plays every scenario in the test repository, then each passes and the lane tags the release.

### Criticality

Critical
